notes: Behavioral evals for the Fathom Analytics skill. Covers both the active instrument-a-site workflow (analyze -> propose -> approval gate -> create via API -> wire code) and the reference-only asks (embed snippet, self-exclude, API query). The workflow evals check that nothing gets created or committed before Matt approves, and that the skill doesn't invent duplicate events or over-propose vanity tracking.

evals.prompt: Set up Fathom tracking for this site. [run inside a client repo with a contact form, a pricing page with a 'Book a call' CTA linking to Calendly, and no existing Fathom embed]
evals.expected_output: Greps for an existing data-site embed first, then checks client-report's clients.json, then asks for the site ID or offers to create one rather than guessing. Analyzes the repo and proposes a small set of decision-worthy events (contact form submitted, booking link clicked) rather than every clickable element. Presents the plan as a table and stops for approval before calling the API or editing any files.
expectations: Follows the layered site-id resolution (grep embed -> client-report registry -> ask/offer to create) rather than assuming a site_id
Proposes events only for genuine decision points (contact form, booking CTA) — does not propose tracking for every button or nav link
Presents the full plan (events, any milestone, instrumentation points) before creating or editing anything
Does not call the Fathom API or write code until Matt approves

evals.prompt: Yes, that plan looks good, go ahead. [approving a previously-shown plan with 2 new events and 1 milestone]
evals.expected_output: Checks GET /sites/{site_id}/events first and skips creating any event that already exists by name. Creates the remaining events via POST, the milestone via POST with a name under 30 characters, then wires the trackEvent() calls using the delegated data-fathom-event listener pattern (or the site's existing behavior layer, if it has one) rather than a bespoke listener per event and without assuming a specific framework. Reports back what was created with Fathom's returned IDs and which files changed.
expectations: Calls GET /sites/{site_id}/events before creating, and skips any pre-existing event by name instead of duplicating it
Keeps the milestone name at or under 30 characters
Uses the shared delegation pattern (data attribute + one listener) rather than one custom listener per tracked element
Reports created event/milestone IDs and the files it changed

evals.prompt: Add a Fathom event for our $49/mo signup so we can see revenue.
evals.expected_output: Uses fathom.trackEvent() with _value in cents (4900), notes currency has to be set in Site settings > Events since the API/JS call doesn't set it, and doesn't invent a cart/funnel model Fathom doesn't have.
expectations: Mentions setting currency separately in the dashboard
Does not fabricate ecommerce funnel steps Fathom doesn't support

evals.prompt: My own visits to the client's site are messing up their Fathom numbers. How do I stop that?
evals.expected_output: Recommends fathom.blockTrackingForMe() run once in the browser console, not IP-based firewall blocking, and explains why (IPs change, this doesn't).
expectations: Recommends fathom.blockTrackingForMe() as the primary fix
Distinguishes this from firewall IP blocking

evals.prompt: Pull last month's total visits and top 10 pages for site ID ABCDE from the Fathom API.
evals.expected_output: Two curl calls against api.usefathom.com/v1/aggregations with a bearer token read from the shared client-report token file: one for totals (visits/uniques/pageviews), one with field_grouping=pathname, sort_by=pageviews:desc, limit=10.
expectations: Includes a totals query and a separate top-pages query with field_grouping=pathname
Reads the token from ~/.config/client-report/fathom-token rather than asking Matt to paste one
Uses date_from/date_to for the specific month
